title: Latency + Error-overlay dashboard for model/route with streaming vs non-streaming segmentation
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create a unified dashboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route with a streaming vs non-streaming (io_mode) breakdown, overlayed with error rates and error classes. The dashboard should help SREs and runtime engineers quickly determine whether latency regressions are correlated with increased errors, IO mode composition shifts, KV cache degradations, or batching changes.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard exposes p50, p95, p99 latency timeseries per model and per route for the last 7d, 30d with selectable time window
Live toggle to split by request.io_mode: 'streaming' vs 'non_streaming' and to show combined view
Error-rate overlay (5m, 1h aggregations) displayed aligned to latency percentile bands
Heatmap panel that buckets request shapes (prompt_tokens x response_tokens) and shows p95 latency and error-rate per bucket
Trace-link integration: each cell/timepoint includes 'open traces' link that launches trace view filtered to the model/route/io_mode
Alert playbook entry added: thresholds for p95 increase + error-rate bump with runbook links
Dashboard reviewed by PM and Design and deployed to console-2026.03 release folder
tech_notes: Use histograms for accurate pX extraction; if histogram buckets insufficient, compute pX via exported tdigest in pipeline
Tag keys: model, route, io_mode, serve_path, model_family, kv_cache_hit
Tracing hooks: add trace annotation 'dashboard.marker' at gateway when request metadata resolved (model/version/route/io_mode)
We will use a composite panel that queries the histogram for percentiles and overlays error-rate time series on secondary axis
dashboard_panels: Top-level timeseries: p50/p95/p99 lines per selected model (multi-select) with stacked error-rate bars
Split view: two vertical panels comparing streaming vs non-streaming for the same route/model selection
Heatmap: request-shape (prompt_len x response_len) showing p95 latency color and error-rate as diagonal hatch
Tail-latency explorer: distribution violin for p99 across routes, with inline sample request IDs
KV-correlation panel: p95 latency grouped by kv_cache_hit(true|false) to surface cache regressions
Alert summary: recent alerts triggered for selected model/route with links to incident and changelog
query_snippets: p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, io_mode))
error_rate: sum(rate(redwood_request_errors_total[5m])) by (model, route, io_mode) / sum(rate(redwood_request_count[5m])) by (model, route, io_mode)
heatmap: quantile_over_time(0.95, redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket{model="$model", route="$route"}[1h]) grouped by prompt_tokens,response_tokens
tracing_changes: Add gateway-level annotation 'resolved_model' and 'resolved_route' to root span before routing decision
Emit io_mode tag (streaming|non_streaming) on every top-level request span
When error occurs, attach 'error_class' tag and sample stack/handler metadata for up to 10k traces/day per service
Add sampling rule for low-latency tail traces: increase sampling for traces where latency > p99 by recent-h1 baseline
log_pipeline_changes: Update log ingestion enrichment to attach model and route tags using the new gateway enrichment service
Create derived metric redwood.request.errors_by_class from logs for error-class heatmaps
Backfill histogram buckets for latency via nightly job for the last 30d to populate dashboard historical view
Add KV cache hit boolean to request logs to enable correlation panels
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy dashboard queries with synthetic data and verify percentile extraction (2 days)
Phase 2 (canary): enable tracing hooks on 10% of requests for a single route and verify trace-links (3 days)
Phase 3 (prod): enable across routing plane, publish dashboard to console-2026.03, and announce to SRE/Runtime teams (1 day)
Fallback: if histogram quantile is noisy, fall back to tdigest-derived percentiles stored in metrics-store
test_plan: Unit tests for query templates and dashboard variable expansion
Integration: generate synthetic workloads (streaming vs non-streaming) and assert p50/p95/p99 track expected ratios
E2E: cause an intentional error class in staging and confirm overlayed error-rate spike and trace-links target correct spans
Load test: ensure dashboard queries return under 3s for 30d range with default filters
risks: High-cardinality tags (model+route+serve_path+io_mode) may increase query cost; mitigate with pre-aggregation for popular model/route combos
Histograms not present for older metrics could make historical percentiles inaccurate; backfill required
Tracing increased sampling may raise storage costs; sampling rules must be bounded
False positives in alerts when traffic mix shifts (e.g., sudden increase in streaming requests)
